cost_anchors.estimate: six small fits (the largest is the 100000-row reproduction rung at about 204 s and M4 on 26346 rows at a few hundred) plus six scorings of 321409 rows and one row-identity scan over every scored row (about 260 s in the smoke); expected well under an hour at 3 threads and nice 10 on 4 cores, no GPU
cost_anchors.launch_minimum: 8.0 GB MemAvailable (0018 needed 14.5 because it materialised an 800000-row pool block; the largest block here is 100000 rows), 0.5 GB disk, 1-minute load under 2.0, no other tools/pivot runner
cost_anchors.source: banked fits on the same machine: artifacts/pivot/deflate_curve.json rungs and artifacts/pivot/oob_4096.json

design.clause: real_model's correct rows over the 38452 real-family rows of 0018's sealed evaluation corpus >= 3402 (chance 1/26 + 0.05), the same bar and the same rows 0018 applied, so the two readings are directly comparable.
design.question: Does the encoder signal exist in real files at all at a 4096-byte carve? 0018/0019 read OOB_TRANSFER_FAILS with a model that had never seen a real file, so that reading cannot separate a training-distribution failure from real content carrying little signal. 0020 changes exactly one thing - what the recipes are fitted on - and holds the scoring set, the recipes, the seed, the bar and the machinery fixed.
design.what_it_is_and_is_not: An IN-DISTRIBUTION reading on real content, not a transfer reading. The fit chunks and the scored chunks are cut from the same five pinned blobs and share no byte, no chunk index, no chunk id and no source-chunk hash, but they are the same files. Every verdict string the reader emits says so.
design.why_now: VERDICT.md says in as many words, in the paragraph published with 0019, that the record 'says nothing about what a recipe fitted on real content would do'. This is the cheapest decisive answer available from data already pinned and audited: no new sources, no new licence work, six small fits.

byte_identity_exclusion.found_by: tools/pivot/corpus_realfit.py --disjoint, written before the corpus was sealed
byte_identity_exclusion.why: a first build (1037 chunks) shared one source-chunk sha256 with the sealed evaluation corpus: two whole 32768-byte chunks of the PE blob are byte-identical runs of padding at different offsets, so index disjointness was not enough and the chunk would have put evaluation rows into the fit block. The selection now drops any candidate whose bytes hash to a sealed chunk's or to an earlier fit chunk's; 2 pe_bin chunks went, both of which had produced no rows, so the row count did not change (26346 either way) and the array hashes are identical.

fit_corpus.selection: every whole 32768-byte chunk of each pinned blob that 0018's sealed selection (n_per_family 300, seed 20260909, recomputed here from tools/pivot/corpus_ext.py) does not use, in blob order, minus every chunk whose bytes hash to a sealed chunk's or to an earlier fit chunk's; no seed of its own

findings_declined.finding: replace the single mixture fit with five per-family in-distribution fits (design lens, recommendation 10)
findings_declined.why: a different experiment, not a fix to this one. It would answer the existence question one family at a time and would be cheaper, but it drops the direct comparability with 0018's banked 2450 correct rows on the same 38452 rows under the same bar, which is the comparison 0020 exists to make. The per-family reading it wants is adopted instead as clause_per_family, published beside the verdict. The five-fit design is worth a later preregistration and is recorded here as one.

findings_declined.finding: seal the fit permutation as chunk-grouped, or switch the recipes' val from 'frag' to 'group', so the early-stopping validation split is not 100% chunk-contaminated (design lens)
findings_declined.why: two of the three reviewers who raised the contamination argued against changing it, and they are right. The recipes are 0014's searched winners and 0018's roster entries verbatim; changing the fitting protocol would break the comparison. The direction of the bias is stated instead and it runs AGAINST the clause: a contaminated split lets early stopping run long, which overfits, which lowers the held-out reading on the chunk-disjoint scoring set. It cannot manufacture a pass. What it can do is widen the real_model versus builder_matched gap, and that is handled by builder_chunk_matched, which measured at the same 1.0 contamination as the fit block against builder_matched's 0.438 - so it matches on the plaintext budget AND on the character of the split. The three measured percentages are banked and iteration counts are flags.

pre_freeze_review.how: Five independent read-only reviewers, one lens each - design and science, the corpus and leakage, the frozen reader, the runner, the gate and the preregistration text - each told to try to break the instrument and to recompute rather than read off. None could write to the repository. They ran for 17 to 24 minutes each and returned 58 findings between them.
pre_freeze_review.reviewer_touches_of_the_sealed_set: One reviewer, testing whether near-duplicate content propagates, computed a 1-nearest-neighbour label transfer from the fit corpus onto 3591 extension rows (500 high-containment, 3091 controls), reading 0.0920 against 0.0880. It tuned nothing - the recipes, the seed, the bar and the row sets were all sealed and hash-pinned, and 1-NN is on no roster - but scope.sealed_set_disclosure counts every touch, so it is counted there and here.
pre_freeze_review.status: complete; findings applied before the freeze
pre_freeze_review.the_finding_that_justified_the_review: THREE REVIEWERS, SEPARATELY, FOUND THE SAME DEFECT: tools/pivot/run_realfit.py never banked a `ledger`, and the generated reader requires exactly one 'completed' ledger event per arm. An honest, complete, valid run would have emitted VOID on six clauses after about an hour of fitting. Two of them then found four more sealed literals in the reader's fit_corpus block taken from the corpus manifest's BUILT counts where the runner measures the with-rows counts - n_chunks 1035 against 1029, pe_bin 207 against 203, py_src 674 against 672, chunk_id_max 20400000 against 20400039 - plus a ceiling_distinct_fragments key the runner never writes. Ten VOID clauses in total on a correct run. One reviewer built a faithful artifact from the runner's own assemble() key set and confirmed it; another demonstrated the converse, that an artifact which MISDESCRIBED the fit corpus passed while the truthful one voided. This is 0018's failure mode exactly, caught before the freeze this time instead of after the run.
pre_freeze_review.what_the_reviewers_checked_and_found_cor: Stated so the report is not read as blanket doubt. All six arm fingerprints recomputed identically through the runner's path and the reader's; every PARTITION and CORPUS literal reproduced from grouped_split on the real cache; the whole ext block reproduced from the npz; the recipes byte-identical to 0018's; the clause arithmetic, the 38452 row count, the 0.165 interpolation and every banked citation reproduced at the precision written; the corpus rebuilt byte-identically from the pinned sources in 170 s with only build_seconds and generated_utc differing; fit and sealed selections disjoint by index, chunk id and source-chunk hash with zero overlap; the two dropped pe_bin chunks confirmed to be the all-zero padding chunks; the label factory imported rather than reimplemented and seeing nothing but the carved bytes; no family's ceiling within a factor of ten of the bar; resume-after-restart byte-identical across a full six-arm rehearsal run twice; scope stated before data; no claimed customer, user, partner or buyer anywhere; the sealed-set ordinal correct; the stated prior genuinely two-sided and discounting its own optimistic arithmetic against interest.
pre_freeze_review.why_the_instruments_could_not_see_it: The 33-case mutation gate was 33/33 green throughout, and the pre-freeze check passed. Both were circular at precisely the wrong values. The gate's control did `dict(r20.FIT)`, `dict(r20.EXT)`, `dict(r20.CORPUS)` and `dict(r20.PARTITION)` - it took the blocks from the READER's literals, which docs/OPERATING_RULES.md section 4 forbids in as many words: 'a control that shares an assumption with the reader cannot see the reader disagree with the world'. It also injected a `ledger` key outright. The one case that asserts that rule computed `set(shape) - set(art)` only - one direction, one level - so an invented key was invisible and so was every nested divergence; and it compared against a committed fixture that was itself already two partition keys stale. The pre-freeze check compared `r20.FIT['arrays'] == P['fit_corpus']['arrays']`, two copies of the same literal, for exactly the fields that were wrong.
